checks.title: Require Kerberos pre-authentication on accounts
checks.prerequisites: RSAT ActiveDirectory module and approved directory read access; run against each in-scope domain and record the domain, DC, time and query errors.
artifacts: Directory objects with the DONT_REQ_PREAUTH flag
Account type, enabled state, owner and effective privileges
steps: Query all account objects for the pre-authentication exemption flag, including disabled accounts and computers.
Resolve each result to an owner and current use; prioritise privileged and service accounts and inspect nested membership.
After an approved configuration fix, repeat the same query and confirm application authentication still works through normal monitoring.
checks.expected: No unexplained pre-authentication exemptions remain. Any returned object requires review; a failed or incomplete query is unknown, not a pass.
checks.limitations: No tickets or password hashes are requested or cracked. A documented exception remains an exposure, not a cleared finding.
checks.vendor_context: Related criteria: PingCastle S-NoPreAuth / S-NoPreAuthAdmin; Purple Knight’s pre-authentication indicator. WACC reviews all account objects, not the vendor scoring model.

checks.title: Disable reversible account password storage
checks.prerequisites: RSAT ActiveDirectory module and approved directory read access; run against each in-scope domain and record the domain, DC, time and query errors.
artifacts: Account flags and resultant password policy
Configuration change and subsequent password-change metadata
steps: Identify objects with the reversible-storage flag; inspect default and fine-grained password policies separately.
Determine whether each affected credential was changed after the storage policy was corrected; inspect timestamps only.
Re-query flags and resultant policy following the approved remediation and verify application compatibility.
checks.expected: Neither account flags nor effective policy enable reversible storage; affected credentials have been replaced under the approved process.
checks.limitations: Removing the flag alone does not prove existing stored material was replaced. Never retrieve password material to test this.
checks.vendor_context: Related criteria: PingCastle S-Reversible / S-C-Reversible; Purple Knight’s reversible-storage indicator.

checks.title: Remove unconstrained delegation from non-DC accounts
checks.statement: Remove unconstrained delegation from non-DC accounts.
checks.prerequisites: RSAT ActiveDirectory module and approved directory read access; run against each in-scope domain and record the domain, DC, time and query errors.
artifacts: Trusted-for-delegation flags, SPNs and account state
Authoritative DC inventory and service dependencies
steps: Query user and computer accounts with unrestricted delegation, retaining disabled accounts in the review.
Join results to the authoritative DC inventory; review non-DC objects, SPNs and service owners rather than excluding computers by name.
Inspect the approved replacement design and retest normal service authentication after any separately approved change.
checks.expected: No non-DC account has unexplained unrestricted delegation; required DC behaviour is identified separately.
checks.limitations: This is a configuration review, not a forced-authentication test. Constrained delegation also needs a separate review.
checks.vendor_context: Related criterion: PingCastle P-UnconstrainedDelegation; Purple Knight’s unrestricted-delegation indicator. WACC does not reproduce the vendor’s exclusions or score.

checks.title: Review constrained delegation targets and RBCD permissions
checks.statement: Review constrained delegation targets and RBCD permissions.
checks.prerequisites: RSAT ActiveDirectory module and approved directory read access; run against each in-scope domain and record the domain, DC, time and query errors.
artifacts: msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo and resource-based delegation descriptors
Resolved SPNs, target accounts and effective writers
steps: Export constrained delegation and resource-based delegation on users and computers; include protocol-transition flags.
Resolve every target SPN and delegated principal, flag missing targets and any path to DCs, KRBTGT or hybrid SSO infrastructure.
Inspect who can change the delegation attributes and DACLs, including nested groups and inherited permissions; compare with approved service flows.
checks.expected: Delegation is confined to justified services and cannot be changed by unapproved principals; high-impact targets require explicit investigation.
checks.limitations: Presence is not automatically compromise. An unresolved descriptor, SID or cross-domain target leaves the conclusion unknown.
checks.vendor_context: Related Purple Knight criteria address delegation to sensitive or missing targets and resource-based delegation.

checks.title: Require LDAP signing on each domain controller
checks.statement: Require LDAP signing on each domain controller.
checks.prerequisites: Approved local registry and effective-policy read access on every DC; a directory read alone may not allow these checks.
artifacts: Per-DC LDAPServerIntegrity value and OS/build
Resultant DC security policy and LDAP diagnostic events
steps: Read the effective signing setting on every writable and read-only DC, including newly promoted servers.
Compare the registry, effective GPO and documented OS behaviour; investigate missing settings rather than assuming the default.
Review unsigned-client events and, in an approved lab, verify a supported signed connection succeeds while an unsigned SASL connection fails.
checks.expected: The effective policy requires signing on every scoped DC and the tested connection behaviour agrees.
checks.limitations: TLS and SASL affect interpretation; do not confuse signing with channel binding. Missing registry data is not proof of a weak or strong effective default.
checks.vendor_context: Related Purple Knight criterion: DC LDAP signing. This check requires enforcement, not only capability.

checks.title: Require LDAP channel binding on domain controllers
checks.statement: Require LDAP channel binding on domain controllers.
checks.prerequisites: Approved local registry and policy read access on each DC; compatible LDAPS clients and a lab for negative tests.
artifacts: Per-DC LdapEnforceChannelBinding and build/patch level
Client compatibility review and channel-binding events
steps: Read the channel-binding setting on each DC and compare it with effective policy and the current Windows version.
Identify clients that cannot supply channel-binding tokens and review owned remediation instead of silently accepting a relaxed setting.
In the lab, verify a compatible TLS/SASL client succeeds and a deliberately incompatible approved test fails; inspect associated DC events.
checks.expected: Required channel binding is enforced across scope, with no unexplained compatibility exclusions.
checks.limitations: Setting 1 checks capable clients but is not equivalent to Always/2. A plain simple-bind test does not exercise all channel-binding cases.
checks.vendor_context: Related Purple Knight criterion: DC LDAP channel binding.

checks.title: Require SMB server signing on domain controllers
checks.statement: Require SMB server signing on domain controllers.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to SMB server configuration on every DC; execute the example locally through an approved administrative session.
artifacts: RequireSecuritySignature value
Effective policy and a normal signed test connection
steps: Read the server-side setting for each DC and compare it with the applied security baseline.
Check that signing is required rather than merely enabled; inspect any policy overriding the baseline.
Use a normal approved client connection to verify negotiation and validate an unsigned negative test only in a lab.
checks.expected: RequireSecuritySignature is true across all DCs and connection evidence agrees.
checks.limitations: Client-side signing and server-side requirements are distinct. This checks SMB signing, not LDAP signing or SMB encryption.
checks.vendor_context: Related criterion: PingCastle A-SMB2SignatureNotRequired; Purple Knight’s SMB-signing indicator.

checks.title: Disable SMBv1 on domain controllers
checks.prerequisites: Approved local SMB configuration read access on every DC.
artifacts: EnableSMB1Protocol value and installed component inventory
Legacy dependency register
steps: Read SMB server configuration on every DC and reconcile with the DC inventory.
Inspect any remaining legacy application dependency and its migration owner.
After an approved removal, repeat the configuration query and confirm normal supported SMB access remains functional.
checks.expected: SMBv1 server support is disabled on each scoped DC.
checks.limitations: Do not enable SMBv1 to construct a negative test. Client feature installation and server protocol availability are separate observations.
checks.vendor_context: Related Purple Knight criterion: SMBv1 on domain controllers.

checks.title: Stop and disable the DC Print Spooler service
checks.statement: Stop and disable the DC Print Spooler service.
checks.prerequisites: Approved local service/CIM read access on each DC; printing dependencies reviewed by the service owner.
artifacts: Spooler state and start mode
Effective service policy and exception history
steps: Read service state and startup configuration on all DCs, including offline exceptions in the coverage record.
Investigate a stopped service that remains configured for automatic/manual start; verify the approved baseline prevents restart.
After the normal change process, re-query and review service-start monitoring without attempting coercion.
checks.expected: The service is stopped and disabled on each scoped DC.
checks.limitations: A query error or inaccessible DC is unknown. This assessment never coerces authentication or extracts credentials.
checks.vendor_context: Related criterion: PingCastle A-DC-Spooler; Purple Knight’s DC Spooler indicator.

checks.title: Review protected-account permission templates
checks.prerequisites: RSAT AD provider and rights to read DACLs; approved baseline of AdminSDHolder and protected groups.
artifacts: AdminSDHolder owner/DACL and inheritance flag
Protected-group memberships and change events
steps: Read the AdminSDHolder security descriptor and compare it with the reviewed baseline.
Resolve every non-default write, ownership and DACL-change permission through nested groups; distinguish read permissions from takeover rights.
Trace deviations to an authorised change and inspect affected protected accounts; confirm the monitoring process detects a benign lab ACL change.
checks.expected: No unexplained writer or inheritance change affects protected accounts; approved customisation is narrowly scoped.
checks.limitations: adminCount alone is not proof an account is currently privileged. A differing ACL needs analysis, not an automatic compromise claim.
checks.vendor_context: Related Purple Knight criteria: changes to AdminSDHolder permissions and inheritance.

checks.title: Review AD CS templates for requester-controlled identities
checks.statement: Review AD CS templates for requester-controlled identities.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to published certificate templates, issuing CA configuration and enrolment ACLs; PKI owner interprets effective rights.
artifacts: Published templates and issuing CAs
Subject-name flags, EKUs, approval/signature requirements
Effective enrolment rights including nested groups
steps: Enumerate templates actually published by issuing CAs and correlate subject-supply options with authentication-capable EKUs.
Check manager approval, authorised-signature requirements and whether an unprivileged principal can effectively enrol.
Have the PKI owner review each dangerous combination and retest configuration after remediation; use synthetic certificate requests only in an isolated lab.
checks.expected: No unapproved low-privilege enrolment path can request an authentication certificate for another identity.
checks.limitations: ESC1 requires a combination of settings and effective access. A single template flag is insufficient, and other ESC classes remain outside this check.
checks.vendor_context: Related Purple Knight criterion: AD CS ESC1. WACC assesses the effective exposure rather than cloning the vendor detector.

checks.title: Review key-credential changes and write permissions
checks.statement: Review key-credential changes and write permissions.
checks.prerequisites: RSAT directory/DACL read access, approved Windows Hello/key-trust design and protected change-event access.
artifacts: Objects with msDS-KeyCredentialLink values
Attribute-write permissions and trusted enrolment identities
5136 change events and key-enrolment records
steps: Inventory objects carrying key-credential values and reconcile them with legitimate enrolment records without exporting private keys.
Inspect explicit and inherited rights to write the attribute or change the object’s DACL; resolve service-account and nested-group access.
Trace unexplained recent modifications to actor and source; in a lab, verify a legitimate enrolment is logged and an unapproved write is denied.
checks.expected: Key registrations and attribute writers are explainable and sensitive changes reach monitoring.
checks.limitations: A non-empty attribute is normal in legitimate key-trust deployments. Do not clear values merely because this inventory returns them.
checks.vendor_context: ASD September 2026 shadow-credential guidance; complementary to public vendor certificate-persistence checks.

checks.title: Verify KRBTGT recovery and credential-rotation readiness
checks.statement: Verify KRBTGT recovery and credential-rotation readiness.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to KRBTGT metadata, replication health, approved rotation history and forest-recovery runbooks.
artifacts: KRBTGT PasswordLastSet and account metadata
Replication health and approved rotation schedule
Isolated forest-recovery exercise record
steps: Compare rotation history with the six-month and suspected-compromise triggers in this control and its ASD/ISM sources. Trace both password changes to change records and replication evidence; PasswordLastSet alone cannot establish that both occurred. Review RODC-specific account procedures separately where applicable.

Check the runbook requires two coordinated password changes, domain-controller replication between changes, and planning for ticket lifetime and replication convergence after suspected compromise or the scheduled interval.
Review or observe an isolated recovery exercise with identity dependencies and validation; do not reset production KRBTGT as a test.
checks.expected: Evidence demonstrates two coordinated KRBTGT password changes within the required six-month interval and after suspected domain compromise, with replication between changes and a tested recovery procedure. Missing change history is unknown, not a pass.
checks.limitations: Age alone does not prove compromise. Rotation without replication and ticket-lifetime planning can disrupt authentication.
checks.vendor_context: Related Purple Knight criterion: KRBTGT credential age. WACC applies the linked ASD/ISM criteria; it does not reproduce the vendor threshold or scoring.

checks.title: Inspect trust boundaries and SID filtering
checks.statement: Inspect trust boundaries and SID filtering.
checks.prerequisites: RSAT AD read access in each trusted domain, trust design and approved migration exceptions.
artifacts: Trust direction/type and SID filtering settings
Selective-authentication and allowed-to-authenticate permissions
Migration exceptions and privileged SID-history review
steps: Inventory all trusts and compare their purpose and direction with approved business relationships.
Assess SID filtering in the context of forest versus external trust semantics; inspect selective authentication and target-system permissions.
Review migration exceptions and privileged SID history with the domain owner; use a synthetic cross-trust account to validate authorised and denied access.
checks.expected: No unexplained trust permits a lower-trust identity to exercise privileged access across the boundary.
checks.limitations: Do not judge a forest trust from SIDFilteringQuarantined alone; forest-aware filtering and migration settings differ.
checks.vendor_context: Complements public vendor trust/SID-filtering criteria; interpretation follows the actual trust type.
